# 1\. Introduction {#1.-introduction}

## 1.1 Purpose {#1.1-purpose}

This document specifies the software requirements for the **Automated Archery Scoring System** — a full-stack application that combines a computer-vision based arrow-detection pipeline with a tournament-management web platform. It is intended for developers, testers, tournament organizers, and reviewers who need a single authoritative reference for *what the system does*, independent of how it is implemented.

## 1.2 Problem Statement {#1.2-problem-statement}

Traditional archery competition management relies heavily on manual observation, presenting critical issues:

1. **Human Error & Dispute Delays**: Disagreements over "line cutters" frequently halt competitions for manual inspection.

2. **High Latency**: Significant delays occur before scores are tallied and shared with spectators and coaches.

3. **High Hardware Cost**: Existing electronic systems require specialized hardware costing thousands of dollars per lane.

4. **Environmental Degradation**: Standard sensors fail under varying outdoor sunlight, camera angles, or worn target faces.

## 1.3 Objectives {#1.3-objectives}

The system aims to achieve the following technical objectives:

* **Sub-2-Second Detection Latency**: Detect target boundaries and identify arrow tips in under 2.0 seconds.

* **World Archery (WA) Compliance**: Implement precise mathematical scoring for Zones 1 to 10 and the X-ring.

* **Multi-Method AI Engine**: Maintain \>95% accuracy using YOLOv8 fused with multi-spectral CV fallbacks.

## 1.4 Scope {#1.4-scope}

* Tournament, session (round), and archer/lane registration management.  
* Connecting physical cameras (USB / RTSP / HTTP) to lanes and streaming live previews.  
* An AI/computer-vision pipeline that detects arrow impact points on a World Archery (WA) standard target face and computes a score (zone 0–10) with a confidence value.  
* Manual validation/override of AI-detected scores with a full audit trail.  
* Real-time leaderboard computation (Redis-cached) and broadcast to all connected clients over WebSocket.  
* Report generation (PDF / CSV / JSON) for sessions and tournaments.  
* Role-based access control (admin, scorer, spectator, archer).  
* System health monitoring (database, cache, storage, thread pool) and audit logging.  
* Out of scope: payment/billing, hardware driver development, mobile native apps (the web frontend is responsive but not a native app), and multi-tenant SaaS isolation (single deployment per venue/tournament is assumed).

# 2\. Overall Description {#2.-overall-description}

## 2.1 Product Perspective {#2.1-product-perspective}

The system is a self-contained client-server application with three runtime tiers:

![][image1]

*Figure 1: System Tiers and Runtime Architecture*

The backend is the system of record; the frontend is a thin presentation layer with no independent business logic. Cameras are the only external hardware dependency.

## 2.2 Product Functions (Summary) {#2.2-product-functions-(summary)}

1. User registration, authentication (JWT) and role-based authorization.

2. Tournament creation and lifecycle management.

3. Session (round) creation, lane configuration, and status transitions (active / paused / completed).

4. Archer registration and lane assignment per session.

5. Camera registration, connection/disconnection, lane assignment, and automatic reconnection.

6. Live camera preview streaming to the frontend.

7. AI-assisted arrow detection and zone/score computation from captured frames.

8. Manual validation or override of AI-computed scores with audit trail.

9. Real-time, cached leaderboard computation and ranking.

10. Real-time event broadcast (score recorded, leaderboard updated, camera/session state changes) via WebSocket.

11. Report generation and export (PDF, CSV, JSON) at session level.

12. System health monitoring (DB, cache, storage, thread pool).

13. Audit logging of significant state-changing actions.

14. Storage quota monitoring and (planned) data retention/archival.

## 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics {#2.3-user-classes-and-characteristics}

The system implements **four roles** at the API/authorization layer (src/dependencies.py, require\_role()), with admin implicitly satisfying any role check:

| Role (implemented) | Conceptual Persona(s) | Description | Typical Access |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| admin | System Administrator \+ Tournament Administrator | Full system access: user management, tournament/session CRUD, camera configuration, all reports, system health | Everything |
| scorer | Scorer / Range Operator | Operates cameras during an active session, triggers AI scoring, confirms/overrides scores | Scoring endpoints, assigned cameras, session data |
| archer | Archer / Competitor | Views own scores, own annotated images, own leaderboard position and personal report | Read-only, scoped to own data |
| spectator | Public viewer | Read-only access to public leaderboard/session info | Read-only, public data |

## 2.4 System Stakeholders {#2.4-system-stakeholders}

The following stakeholders are involved in the system:

* **Archery Athletes / Competitors**: Primary subjects who shoot arrows and rely on instant, fair scoring and immediate feedback.  
* **Event Scorers & Umpires**: Field officials responsible for supervising sessions, reviewing low-confidence AI detections, and resolving disputes.  
* **Tournament Administrators**: Event hosts who configure tournaments, setup sessions, assign lanes/cameras, and manage permissions.  
* **Spectators & Audience**: Remote and stadium fans who view real-time leaderboards and shot placements.  
* **Software & AI Engineers**: Maintainers responsible for model training, pipeline optimization, and system uptime.

## 2.5 Operating Environment {#2.5-operating-environment}

* **Backend**: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, runs behind Uvicorn; PostgreSQL 15+ for persistence; Redis for caching/pub-sub support; optional OpenCV (cv2) for computer vision the arrow-detection service degrades gracefully if OpenCV is not installed.

* **Frontend**: React 18 \+ TypeScript SPA built with Vite, served as static assets; targets modern desktop and tablet browsers (Chromium/Firefox/Safari).

* **Deployment**: Docker Compose (db, cache, api services) for local/venue deployment; Alembic manages schema migrations.

* **Hardware**: USB UVC cameras, RTSP IP cameras, or HTTP/MJPEG cameras, one per shooting lane.

## 2.6 Design and Implementation Constraints {#2.6-design-and-implementation-constraints}

* All business logic must live in the service layer; API routers must not access the ORM directly (layering constraint already enforced in the codebase).

* All configurable values (pool sizes, JWT TTL, rate limits, image processing parameters, WebSocket batching) must be sourced from Settings (src/config.py), not hard-coded.

* Score and audit records are immutable once written — corrections are recorded as **overrides**, not as deletions/updates of history.

* The event bus (src/events.py) is in-process, fire-and-forget; it is **not** a durable message queue. Consumers (leaderboard cache invalidation, WebSocket broadcast, audit log) must tolerate at-most-once delivery.

## 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies {#2.7-assumptions-and-dependencies}

* A reasonably well-lit, stationary target face is assumed for the CV pipeline to achieve target confidence levels.

* Network connectivity between cameras and backend is assumed to be local (LAN), not over the public internet, to meet the \<1s scoring latency target.

* Exactly one archer and one camera are bound to a lane within a given session at a time.

| **FR-06** | **Image Acquisition** | The system shall capture target images either manually, periodically, or automatically based on configurable triggers. Captured images shall be associated with the corresponding tournament, session, lane, archer, end, and arrow sequence. The scoring engine shall assign values from **0 to 10**, detect **X-ring** hits, support configurable target dimensions, and calculate cumulative scores for ends, sets, sessions, and tournaments. | High |
| **FR-09** | **Manual Score Validation & Override** | Authorized users (Admin and Scorer) shall be able to review AI-generated scores using annotated target images displaying detected arrows, scoring rings, impact coordinates, and confidence values. | **FR-10** | **Real-Time Score Broadcasting** | The system shall publish score updates instantly through WebSocket connections whenever a score is generated or modified. | **FR-11** | **Leaderboard & Ranking** | The system shall continuously compute live rankings based on cumulative scores, X-counts, tie-breaking rules, and tournament-specific ranking policies. Frequently accessed leaderboard data shall be cached using Redis to reduce database load. Cache entries shall be automatically invalidated and regenerated whenever scores are added, updated, or removed. | Medium |

| **FR-13** | **Audit Logging & System Monitoring** | The system shall record all critical administrative operations including user authentication, tournament modifications, score overrides, camera configuration changes, AI processing events, and system configuration updates in an immutable audit log. | **FR-14** | **Image Storage** | The system shall securely store original captured images, processed images, and annotated images while maintaining references to tournament, session, lane, and archer information. | Medium |
| **FR-15** | **AI Processing Queue** | The system shall process image scoring requests asynchronously using a task queue to support concurrent scoring from multiple shooting lanes. | Medium |
| **FR-16** | **Notifications** | The system shall notify scorers when image processing fails, cameras disconnect, or manual validation is required. | Medium |

# 6\. AI Engineering Design {#6.-ai-engineering-design}

##  6.1 Multi-Stage Computer Vision & AI Pipeline {#6.1-multi-stage-computer-vision-&-ai-pipeline}

The system utilizes a 5-stage hybrid processing pipeline combining computer vision heuristics and deep learning:

* **Stage 1: Preprocessing**: Includes dynamic rescaling, CLAHE contrast enhancement, and bilateral filter denoising.

* **Stage 2: Target Detection**: Localizes the target face using zone ellipses fitting, color bands masking, and HoughCircles fallback.

* **Stage 3: Arrow Detection**: Employs concurrent strategies including Puncture Hole Blackhat Morphology, Color Segmentation, Multi-Channel HoughLinesP, SIFT Keypoint Analysis, and YOLOv8 inference.

* **Stage 4: Zone & Ellipse Scoring**: Uses line-ellipse intersection algorithms and normalized radial distance calculations mapped to WA standards.

* **Stage 5: Confidence Fusion**: Calculates a composite confidence score to validate AI results or flag for manual review.


## 6.2 Heuristic Rules Engine & Mathematical Scoring Formulations {#6.2-heuristic-rules-engine-&-mathematical-scoring-formulations}

**Color Threshold Specifications**

* **Yellow / Gold (Bullseye & 9-Ring)**: HSV: H ∈ \[13, 45\], S ∈ \[70, 255\], V ∈ \[100, 255\]; LAB: L ∈ \[0, 255\], A ∈ \[0, 255\], B \> 143\.

* **Red (8 & 7 Rings)**: HSV Range 1: H ∈ \[0, 14\], S ∈ \[90, 255\], V ∈ \[70, 255\]; HSV Range 2: H ∈ \[163, 180\], S ∈ \[90, 255\], V ∈ \[70, 255\]; LAB: A \> 140\.

* **Blue (6 & 5 Rings)**: HSV: H ∈ \[85, 140\], S ∈ \[90, 255\], V ∈ \[60, 255\].

* **Black (4 & 3 Rings)**: HSV: H ∈ \[0, 180\], S ∈ \[0, 255\], V ∈ \[15, 110\].

* **White (2 & 1 Rings)**: HSV: H ∈ \[0, 180\], S ∈ \[0, 40\], V ∈ \[190, 255\].

**Mathematical Intersection Formula (Quadratic Substitution Method)**

The system solves for entry intersection using the quadratic equation *At² \+ Bt \+ C \= 0*, where A, B, and C are derived from the line segment components substituted into the canonical ellipse equation. Roots are solved to find the entry point (t) representing the shaft's intersection with the target plane.

**WA Zone Radial Mapping**

| Normalized Distance (d\_norm) | Scoring Zone |
| :---- | :---- |
| ≤ 0.048 | Zone 10 (X-Ring) |
| ≤ 0.096 | Zone 10 (Outer Gold) |
| ≤ 0.192 | Zone 9 (Yellow) |
| ≤ 0.288 / 0.384 | Zone 8 / 7 (Red) |
| ≤ 0.480 / 0.576 | Zone 6 / 5 (Blue) |
| ≤ 0.672 / 0.768 | Zone 4 / 3 (Black) |
| ≤ 0.864 / 0.960 | Zone 2 / 1 (White) |
| \> 0.960 | Zone 0 (Miss) |

The 'Automated Archery Scoring System' boundary contains use cases: Manage Users, Manage Tournaments, Manage Sessions, Register Archers, Configure Cameras, View Live Camera Preview, Trigger AI Scoring (includes Review Detected Score and Confirm Score, extends Override Score), View Override History, View Real-Time Leaderboard, View Own Scores & Report, Receive Real-Time Notifications, Monitor System Health, and Generate/Export Report. Connections: The Admin persona connects to ALL use cases including those shared with the Scorer (Trigger AI Scoring, View Live Camera Preview, View Override History, View Real-Time Leaderboard) and Admin-specific ones (Manage Users, Manage Tournaments, Manage Sessions, Configure Cameras, Monitor System Health, Generate/Export Report). The Archer connects to View Real-Time Leaderboard, View Own Scores & Report, and Receive Real-Time Notifications. The Spectator connects to View Real-Time Leaderboard and Receive Real-Time Notifications.][image2]

## 7.1.2 Use Case Descriptions {#7.1.2-use-case-descriptions}

### UC-01: Manage Users {#uc-01:-manage-users}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Administrative control over user accounts and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) levels.

* **Flow:** Admin creates or deactivates accounts, assigns roles, and updates profile information; system enforces uniqueness and hashes passwords.

### UC-02: Manage Tournaments {#uc-02:-manage-tournaments}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Creation and lifecycle management of high-level tournament events.

* **Flow:** Admin inputs tournament metadata (name, location, dates); system validates timing constraints and persists the tournament state.

### UC-03: Manage Sessions {#uc-03:-manage-sessions}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Configuration of shooting rounds and control of session status (active, paused, completed).

* **Flow:** Admin initializes a round within a tournament; system manages state transitions and enforces session-specific scoring rules.

### UC-04: Register Archers {#uc-04:-register-archers}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Assignment of archers to specific shooting lanes for a given session.

* **Flow:** Admin maps archer names to lane numbers; system validates that lanes are not double-assigned within the same session.

### UC-05: Configure Cameras {#uc-05:-configure-cameras}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Registration and mapping of physical cameras (USB/RTSP/HTTP) to shooting lanes.

* **Flow:** Admin provides camera connection parameters; system establishes stream connectivity and initiates heartbeat monitoring.

### UC-06: View Live Camera Preview {#uc-06:-view-live-camera-preview}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin, Scorer.

* **Description:** Monitoring of live streams from cameras assigned to lane targets.

* **Flow:** Scorer selects a lane; system streams frames from the backend directly to the browser UI dashboard.

### UC-07: Trigger AI Scoring {#uc-07:-trigger-ai-scoring}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin, Scorer.

* **Description:** Execution of the computer vision pipeline to detect arrow impacts and compute zone scores.

* **Flow:** Scorer triggers capture; system processes frames through target/arrow detection modules and returns a predicted score for review.

### UC-08: View Override History {#uc-08:-view-override-history}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin, Scorer.

* **Description:** Auditing of manual score corrections and the rationale behind them.

* **Flow:** User filters audit logs by archer or lane; system displays original detected points vs. manually entered points and reasons.

### UC-09: View Real-Time Leaderboard {#uc-09:-view-real-time-leaderboard}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin, Scorer, Archer, Spectator.

* **Description:** Accessing live standings and ranking updates powered by high-performance caching.

* **Flow:** User opens the leaderboard view; system serves current rankings from Redis and refreshes automatically as new scores are recorded.

### UC-10: View Own Scores & Report {#uc-10:-view-own-scores-&-report}

* **Primary Actor:** Archer.

* **Description:** Personal access for competitors to review their individual performance and download scorecards.

* **Flow:** Authenticated archer retrieves their session history; system scopes data to the specific user and provides export options.

### UC-11: Receive Real-Time Notifications {#uc-11:-receive-real-time-notifications}

* **Primary Actor:** Archer, Spectator.

* **Description:** Push updates for score submission, leaderboard changes, and session status shifts.

* **Flow:** System detects state changes; EventBus publishes messages to the WebSocket server which broadcasts updates to all active client connections.

### UC-12: Monitor System Health {#uc-12:-monitor-system-health}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Real-time observation of database pool saturation, storage usage, and service availability.

* **Flow:** Admin accesses health dashboard; system queries component metrics and displays utilization percentages and status indicators.

### UC-13: Generate/Export Report {#uc-13:-generate/export-report}

* **Primary Actor:** Admin.

* **Description:** Production of official session analytics and printable PDF scorecards for tournament archives.

* **Flow:** Admin selects session and format; ReportService aggregates data and streams the generated binary file back to the browser.

### 7.4.1 User Login {#7.4.1-user-login}

![High-fidelity Sequence Diagram: User Login. 1. Frontend sends credentials to API. 2. API calls AuthService. 3. AuthService queries Database to verify user/password. 4. ### 7.4.2 Live AI-Assisted Scoring (Core Flow)   {#7.4.2-live-ai-assisted-scoring-(core-flow)}

![High-fidelity Sequence Diagram: AI Scoring Flow (5-Stage Pipeline). 1. API triggers ScoringService. 2. ScoringService requests frame from Camera. 3. Image sent to DetectionEngine (Stage 1: Preprocessing). 4. Stage 2: Target Detection (Ellipse fitting). 5. Stage 3: Arrow Detection (Multi-strategy fusion). 6. Stage 4: Zone & Ellipse Scoring (Radial mapping). 7. Stage 5: Confidence Fusion. 8. ScoringService writes results to Database. 9. ScoringService notifies EventBus. 10. EventBus triggers WebSocket broadcast to Frontend.][image9]

ScoringService updates score and total\_score in Database. 5. ScoringService records entry in Audit Logs. 6. EventBus invalidates Redis cache. 7. EventBus broadcasts update via WebSocket to all clients.][image10]

*Figure 8: Sequence Diagram \- Score Override*

# 8\. Preliminary Test Plan {#8.-preliminary-test-plan}

## 8.1 Testing Objectives {#8.1-testing-objectives}

The test plan ensures the reliability and accuracy of the automated scoring system through systematic verification.

## 8.2 Features to be Tested {#8.2-features-to-be-tested}

Tested features include core backend REST endpoints, the AI/CV detection pipeline accuracy, and real-time frontend dashboard responsiveness.

## 8.3 Automated Verification Suite {#8.3-automated-verification-suite}

The system includes a pytest verification suite with over 46 unit and integration tests, achieving comprehensive code coverage for the scoring engine.

**Test Matrix Overview**

| Test Module | Sub-Features Tested | Count |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Auth & Security | Registration, JWT Login, Permissions | 6 |
| Tournament Workflow | Creation, Session Init, Archer Registration | 8 |
| Score Engine & CV | Ellipse Detection, Subpixel Tip, WA Mapping | 12 |
| Scoring DB & Retries | Transactional Writes, Backoff Loops | 6 |
| Camera & Streams | Connect/Disconnect, Heartbeats | 5 |
| Leaderboard & Redis | Sorting, Cache Writes/Invalidation | 5 |
| Reports & Export | PDF/CSV Generation | 4 |

## REST API Endpoint Summary {#rest-api-endpoint-summary}

| Domain Router | HTTP Method | Endpoint URI | Purpose / Functional Handler | Role Level |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Authentication** | POST | /api/auth/register | Register new user account (default spectator) | Public |
|  | POST | /api/auth/login | Authenticate credentials & issue JWT token | Public |
|  | POST | /api/auth/refresh | Refresh expired JWT token | Authenticated |
|  | POST | /api/auth/reset-password | Reset user password credentials | Authenticated |
| **Tournaments** | GET | /api/tournaments | List all active/archived tournaments | Public |
|  | POST | /api/tournaments | Create new tournament container | Admin, Scorer |
|  | GET | /api/tournaments/{id} | Retrieve specific tournament metadata | Public |
|  | PUT | /api/tournaments/{id} | Update tournament parameters | Admin, Scorer |
| **Sessions** | GET | /api/tournaments/{id}/sessions | List shooting sessions in tournament | Public |
|  | POST | /api/tournaments/{id}/sessions | Create new round/session (lanes=6) | Admin, Scorer |
|  | GET | /api/sessions/{id} | Retrieve session status & details | Public |
|  | PATCH | /api/sessions/{id} | Update status (active, paused, completed) | Admin, Scorer |
|  | POST | /api/sessions/{id}/archers | Register archer & assign lane number | Admin, Scorer |
| **Scores** | POST | /api/sessions/{id}/scores | Record manual arrow score entry | Scorer |
|  | POST | /api/sessions/{id}/scores/upload | Upload image ![][image16] AI detect ![][image16] score shot | Scorer, System |
|  | GET | /api/sessions/{id}/scores | List all recorded scores for session | Public |
|  | GET | /api/scores/{id} | Retrieve single arrow score record | Public |
|  | POST | /api/scores/{id}/validate | Flag score AI validation status | Scorer |
|  | PUT | /api/scores/{id}/override | Admin/Scorer score override & audit log | Admin, Scorer |
| **Cameras** | GET | /api/sessions/{id}/cameras | List camera streams assigned to session | Admin, Scorer |
|  | POST | /api/sessions/{id}/cameras/{cam\_id}/connect | Connect physical USB/RTSP camera stream | Admin, Scorer |
|  | POST | /api/sessions/{id}/cameras/{cam\_id}/disconnect | Disconnect camera feed | Admin, Scorer |
|  | POST | /api/cameras/{id}/reconnect | Auto-reconnect lost RTSP stream | System, Admin |
|  | POST | /api/sessions/{id}/cameras/assign | Assign camera device to target lane | Admin, Scorer |
| **Leaderboard** | GET | /api/sessions/{id}/leaderboard | Retrieve live sorted leaderboard (Redis cached) | Public |
| **Reports** | GET | /api/sessions/{id}/report | Generate PDF scorecard or CSV export | Public |
| **Health** | GET | /api/health | Basic system health check | Public |
|  | GET | /api/health/detailed | Subsystem status (DB, Redis, Storage) | Admin |
| **Real-Time WS** | WS | /ws/{session\_id} | WebSocket pub/sub live score broadcast | Public |

# 10\. Project Timeline {#10.-project-timeline}

## 10.1 Project Work Breakdown {#10.1-project-work-breakdown}

The project follows an agile 13-week software design and implementation lifecycle:

* **Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4)**: System Specifications, Requirements, Architecture Design, and DB Schema Design.

* **Phase 2 (Weeks 5-11)**: Backend API (FastAPI), Computer Vision Engine, and Frontend Dashboard (React/Vite).

* **Phase 3 (Weeks 10-12)**: AI Model Fine-tuning, WebSocket PubSub, and Redis Caching.

* **Phase 4 (Week 12-13)**: Verification, Automated Testing, Containerization, and Midterm Submission.

![Professional Gantt chart for the 13-week Automated Archery Scoring System project. The timeline is divided into four distinct color-coded phases. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4): 'Requirements Analysis' (W1-2) and 'Architecture & Schema Design' (W2-4). Phase 2 (Weeks 5-11): 'Backend API & Service Layer' (W5-7), 'CV/AI Pipeline Development' (W7-9), and 'Frontend Dashboard UI' (W9-11). Phase 3 (Weeks 10-12): 'Redis Caching & PubSub' (W10-11) and 'AI Model Fine-tuning' (W11-12). Phase 4 (Weeks 12-13): 'Verification & Testing' (W12), 'Containerization & Deployment' (W12), and 'Final Documentation' (W13). # 11\. Conclusion {#11.-conclusion}

The Automated Archery Scoring System represents a significant technological advancement in sports officiating by integrating real-time computer vision with robust tournament management. By addressing the critical challenges of human error, high latency, and hardware costs, this system provides a scalable and reliable solution for modern archery competitions. The proposed architecture, combining a multi-stage AI pipeline with a responsive web-based platform, ensures precise scoring while maintaining system maintainability. Future work will focus on further optimizing detection accuracy under extreme environmental conditions and expanding hardware compatibility.
